state.case_summary:
A 52-year-old Japanese woman presented with a 2-year history of swelling of her right upper eyelid, which had discharged pus for the previous 10 months without any trauma to her head. She was otherwise healthy. She denied any symptoms, including fever, headache, or nasal discharge.

Physical examination revealed an immovable scarlike node, 11 × 7 mm, on her right upper eyelid discharging pus.

- Imaging Studies:    1. MRI findings:       - Title: T2-weighted and contrast-enhanced MRI       - Description: High signal on T2-weighted image and ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus without any abnormal lesions in the orbital or intracranial tissue        2. CT findings:       - Title: Axial and coronal CT sections       - Description: Opacification on right frontal sinus, right ethmoid sinus, and right maxillary sinus and expansion of the right frontal sinus and right ethmoid sinus without any bone destruction        - Histopathology:       - Title: Sinus mucosa examination       - Description: Mild inflammatory infiltrate with fibrosis, lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate, few eosinophils and no sign of malignancy

root.label: Chronic Unilateral Periorbital Swelling with Pus Discharge and Sinus Opacification
supporting_facts: 2-year history of swelling of the right upper eyelid
immovable scarlike node on the right upper eyelid
MRI and CT findings of sinus opacification and expansion
excluded_candidates: Infectious sinusitis: reason ranked lower due to lack of systemic symptoms and negative histopathology for malignancy
Malignant tumor: reason ranked lower due to absence of malignant cells on histopathology

B1.label: Chronic Sinusitis with Cutaneous Fistula
askable_discriminators: Is there a history of nasal discharge or sinus pressure?
requestable_discriminators: CT or MRI of the sinuses

B2.label: Granulomatous Disease with Cutaneous Involvement
askable_discriminators: Is there a history of systemic symptoms such as fever or weight loss?

B3.label: Neoplastic Disease with Sinus Involvement
askable_discriminators: Is there a history of cancer or recent unexplained weight loss?
requestable_discriminators: Imaging studies with contrast, biopsy of the affected tissue

B4.label: Infectious Disease with Cutaneous and Sinus Involvement
askable_discriminators: Is there a history of recent travel or exposure to infectious diseases?
requestable_discriminators: Cultures of the discharge, serological tests

MRI findings: high signal on T2-weighted image and ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus
No abnormal lesions in the orbital or intracranial tissue on MRI
CT findings: opacification on right frontal sinus, right ethmoid sinus, and right maxillary sinus
CT findings: expansion of the right frontal sinus and right ethmoid sinus without any bone destruction

No sign of malignancy on histopathology
